title: Pelau
subtitle: Trinidadian one-pot rice with chicken, pigeon peas, and coconut milk
excerpt: The beloved Trinidadian one-pot national dish: chicken browned in burnt sugar (browning sauce), then cooked with pigeon peas, long-grain rice, coconut milk, and thyme until the rice has absorbed everything. Rich, deeply savoury, and endlessly comforting.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pelau is the national dish of Trinidad and Tobago and one of the most beloved one-pot dishes of the English-speaking Caribbean. Its origins are complex: the dish draws on the Indian pilau (which arrived with Indian indenture workers) combined with African one-pot cooking traditions and local Caribbean ingredients. The distinguishing technique is the browning of the chicken in caramelised sugar — either burnt sugar made at home or browning sauce (a commercial Trinidadian product similar to but more intensely flavoured than Worcestershire sauce) — which gives the finished dish its characteristic dark colour and deep, slightly bitter-sweet flavour. Coconut milk, pigeon peas, and thyme are consistent across virtually all Trinidadian pelau recipes; the exact quantities and spicing vary by household.

recipeTools.notes: A large, heavy casserole or Dutch oven with a tight lid.

content.text: The browning is what makes pelau pelau: burning the sugar dark before adding the chicken gives the dish its colour and depth. The sugar must be cooked until it is very dark (almost black) and smoking slightly; the finished dish should taste savoury and bitter-sweet, not caramel-sweet. Use browning sauce if you have it; it adds complexity. Do not lift the lid during the final rice-cooking stage.

items.preparation: bone-in, skin-on; marinated if time allows with garlic, thyme, salt, pepper
Trinidadian browning sauce, or dark soy sauce as a substitute

content.text: Add the caster sugar to a large, dry casserole over high heat. Let it melt and cook, without stirring, until it turns very dark brown and begins to smoke. Add the oil (it will spit), then immediately add the chicken pieces. Stir to coat in the burnt sugar and brown on all sides over high heat, about 5 minutes. Add the browning sauce.

Add the onion, garlic, spring onions, carrot, and thyme. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring. Add the pigeon peas, coconut milk, and 500 ml of water. Add the whole scotch bonnet. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes.

Stir in the rinsed rice. Bring back to a simmer, cover tightly, and cook on the lowest possible heat for 25 minutes without lifting the lid. Remove from the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes. Remove the scotch bonnet and thyme sprigs. Fluff with a fork and serve.
